topic: Right-triangle trigonometry --- diagnosing wrong-ratio, inverse and degree-mode errors

traps.desc: used cosine where sine was needed, pairing the opposite side with the adjacent ratio

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the wanted side is opposite the given angle while the known side is the hypotenuse, and that pairing is sine, not cosine; cosine would have produced the side adjacent to the angle instead. Full credit requires naming which side each ratio actually returns.

traps.desc: left the calculator in radian mode, so the 52 was read as 52 radians

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the calculator was in radian mode, so the 52 was interpreted as 52 radians rather than 52 degrees. Full credit also requires the student to point out the impossibility that gives it away --- a side of a triangle cannot have a negative length, and no side can be longer than the hypotenuse.

traps.desc: used the inverse tangent although the two known sides were the opposite side and the hypotenuse

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the two known sides are the side opposite the angle and the hypotenuse, which is the sine pairing, so the angle comes from the inverse sine; the inverse tangent would only be right if the second known side were the adjacent one. Full credit requires the pairing to be named, not just the corrected number.

traps.desc: reported the ratio itself as the angle and never applied the inverse cosine

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the division produced the cosine of the angle, not the angle, and that the inverse cosine still has to be applied to undo it. Full credit also requires a reason the answer is impossible on sight: an acute angle of a triangle cannot measure a fraction of one degree when the two sides are so close in length.

traps.desc: left the calculator in radian mode, so the 38 was read as 38 radians

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the calculator was in radian mode, so the 38 was treated as 38 radians. Full credit requires an estimate that exposes it --- a 38 degree angle is a bit more than a third of a right angle, so the rise should be a bit under two thirds of the 24 m cable, nowhere near the printed value.

traps.desc: used tangent, which returns the other leg rather than the hypotenuse

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says tangent relates the two legs, so it can never produce the hypotenuse; with the adjacent side and the angle known, the hypotenuse comes from cosine, with the unknown underneath so the division runs the other way. Full credit also requires the size check: the hypotenuse is the longest side, so any answer shorter than the 26 ft leg is impossible.
